title: Marginal contribution smoothing + contract phasing model
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet models how staggered contract phases (monthly, quarterly, annual) with differing price tiers affect marginal contribution (revenue less incremental hosting and hiring costs) and how a hiring-smoothing policy can reduce short-term margin volatility while preserving long-term unit economics.

Summary of approach (short):
- Build 3 contract phasing products: On-demand (pay-as-you-go), Reserved Quarterly, Reserved Annual (deepest discount).
- Model customer migration mix across products under three price-change scenarios (base, price-up, price-down).
- For each scenario compute: incremental revenue, incremental infra cost (GPU & storage), incremental support & SRE costs (headcount portion), resulting marginal contribution.
- Add headcount smoothing policy: hire in smaller increments; use temporary contractor pool vs FTE; measure incremental cost to smooth.

Key assumptions (editable parameters):
- Base token price (hosted generation): $0.010 per 1k tokens.
- Quarterly discount: 10% vs base; Annual discount: 22% vs base.
- On-demand elasticity: -0.30 (10% price increase => 3% demand drop).
- Reserved customer stickiness: low elasticity (assume -0.05).
- Average tokens per active customer / month: 120M tokens.
- GPU infra marginal cost: $0.0009 per 1k tokens equivalent (includes amortized GPU + storage + networking).
- Support/SRE marginal cost per 1k tokens at scale: $0.0006 (function of routing complexity and SLAs).
- Avg cost of hiring an FTE (fully loaded): $220k/year. Contractor equivalent monthly fully loaded: $18k/month.
- Hiring lead time: 10 weeks to onboard a production engineer. Contractor ramp: 2 weeks.
- Target headcount smoothing: avoid >3 FTE hires in any rolling 60-day window.

Scenarios (high level):
- Scenario BASE: current mix 65% On-demand, 25% Quarterly, 10% Annual. No price change. Growth +7%/month baseline.
- Scenario PRICE_SHOCK_UP: increase base price by +12%. Model demand elasticity per product. Assume 8% churn from On-demand and small churn from reserved.
- Scenario PRICE_DISCOUNT: decrease base price by -15% to acquire share. Assume uplift in On-demand usage +18% and some migration from reserved to cheaper annual.

Illustrative per-customer monthly P&L (simplified units in $k):
- Inputs per representative mid-size customer (120M tokens/mo):
  - Revenue_on_demand = (120M / 1k) * 0.010 = $1,200
  - Revenue_quarterly = revenue_on_demand * 0.90 = $1,080
  - Revenue_annual = revenue_on_demand * 0.78 = $936
  - Infra_cost = (120M / 1k) * 0.0009 = $108
  - Support_cost = (120M / 1k) * 0.0006 = $72
  - Direct_margin_on_demand = 1,200 - (108 + 72) = $1,020

Portfolio-level snapshot (10k customers split by mix):
- BASE mix: 6,500 On-demand, 2,500 Quarterly, 1,000 Annual.
- Base monthly revenue = (6,500*1,200) + (2,500*1,080) + (1,000*936) = $9. + calculate: 6,500*1,200=7,800,000; 2,500*1,080=2,700,000; 1,000*936=936,000 => total = 11,436,000 (~$11.436M).
- Base infra cost = 10k * 108 = $1,080,000. Support cost = 10k * 72 = $720,000.
- Base contribution = 11,436,000 - (1,080,000 + 720,000) = $9,636,000.

PRICE_SHOCK_UP example (12% price increase):
- New on-demand price = 0.0112 per 1k tokens => per-customer rev = 1,344.
- Elasticity applied => demand change for on-demand -3.6% => lost 234 customers from on-demand bucket in 10k cohort, assume migration proportions to reserved negligible short-term.
- Revenue delta rough calc: on-demand revenue = 6,266 * 1,344 = 8,423,904 (vs previous 7,800,000). Gains offset by churn elsewhere; re-run portfolio model to compute net.
- Infra cost increases slightly as price increase does not change tokens consumed by reserved customers but net token volume drops small.
- Result: contribution margin moves up per remaining on-demand customer but absolute total contribution might decline slightly due to churn and fixed headcount.

Smoothing & hiring policy simulation (toy example):
- Without smoothing: to support 10% forecasted growth next quarter, plan to hire 15 FTEs immediately (cost impact: 15 * 220k/12 = $275k/month incremental).
- With smoothing: hire 6 FTEs + 9 contractors for first 3 months => immediate incremental cost = (6*220k/12) + (9*18k) = 110k + 162k = $272k (roughly similar near-term) but contractors can be ramped down if price shock occurs, reducing downside.
- Net present value of smoothing over 6 months assuming 25% chance of price shock: smoothing reduces expected downside by ~ $420k (numeric depends on model runs).

Sensitivity lattice (recommended grid to run):
- X-axis: price change [%] from -25% to +25% in 5% steps.
- Y-axis: reserve penetration shift (Annual+Quarterly mix change) from -10pp to +10pp in 2pp steps.
- For each cell compute: total revenue, infra cost, support cost, headcount incremental cost (baseline hiring plan) and contribution. Store delta vs BASE.

Quick example outputs to look for (what makes smoothing useful):
- Regions where price_up > +10% but reserve penetration falls by >3pp => contribution volatility high and smoothing yields >5% reduction in downside.
- Regions where price_down < -10% and On-demand usage increases >12% => infra cost rises faster than revenue (because reserved yields better margin), suggesting focus on converting high-usage customers to annual with incentives.

Action recommendations (working):
1) Institutionalize a 60-day hiring rate cap for production infra/serving hires; prefer contractors up to 40% of near-term run rate to limit fixed cost exposure.
2) Offer limited-time "annual migration credit" for high-usage on-demand customers to lock-in better unit economics when running a price-discount acquisition window. Track cohort-level LTV vs payback.
3) Add a pricing circuit-breaker in the rate change playbook: if forecasted contribution variance > 4% vs baseline, pause discretionary hiring and trigger contractor-only hires for 30 days.
4) Build automated lattice reports (weekly): delta-contribution heatmap across price and reserve penetration dimensions; link to product experiments and sales incentives.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need more granular token distribution by customer decile (top 1% customers drive outsized infra). Current model uses mean token per customer; decile-aware model will change sensitivity markedly.
- Validate contractor fully-loaded cost assumptions with People Ops and Legal (benefits/agency fees).
- Integrate Dedicated (Reserved Dedicated pools) margin differences: that product's infra marginal cost currently modeled equal to hosted (0.0009) but for Dedicated it's likely higher — adjust.

Next steps (owners):
- Finance: run full lattice and attach detailed CSV output (owner: Rajesh) due 2026-07-29.
- People Ops: confirm contractor cost band and ramp constraints (owner: Maya) due 2026-07-20.
- Product & Sales: validate migration incentive design and legal constraints (owners: Liam & Sofia) due 2026-08-05.
